extracted.intended_audience: PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospitals (PCHs), hospital quality reporting staff and administrators, EHR/health IT vendors, and other CMS program stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and proposed rule provisions describing which electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs) PCHs must report, how and when to submit them, technical and certification requirements, measure specifications (example: Malnutrition Care Score), exemptions, and public reporting policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reporting timing for Hospital Harm eCQMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination, Hospital Harm eCQMs that have not yet been finalized for mandatory reporting would become mandatory in the third year of reporting. Newly adopted Hospital Harm eCQMs would become mandatory eCQMs for reporting after 2 years of self-selected reporting in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples: Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury and Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure would begin mandatory reporting in CY 2028/FY 2030; Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE would become mandatory beginning with the CY 2030 reporting period/FY 2032 after being available for 2 years of self-selected reporting. The proposal builds on a phased approach and assumes hospitals self-select measures where they perform better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malnutrition Care Score eCQM — measure overview
rubrics_metrics.description: The Malnutrition Care Score eCQM assesses the percentage of adults (age 18+) with length of stay ≥24 hours who received optimal malnutrition care appropriate to malnutrition risk and severity, including screening, RD/RDN assessment, physician/clinician diagnosis for moderate/severe malnutrition, and a nutrition care plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted into Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting and Medicare Promoting Interoperability Programs as selectable starting CY 2024; proposed mandatory reporting in PCH and Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting beginning CY 2028/FY 2030 for PCHs. Rationale: high prevalence and adverse outcomes among cancer patients; measure was recommended by Pre-Rulemaking and conditionally endorsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malnutrition Care Score eCQM — measure calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The eCQM consists of four components scored separately: (1) screening at admission; (2) nutrition assessment for those who screened at risk; (3) documentation of malnutrition diagnosis if assessment indicates moderate/severe malnutrition; (4) development of a nutrition care plan. Each eligible component is scored 0 (not documented) or 1 (documented); component values are summed to form the numerator. The denominator is the total eligible occurrences of the four components for patients 18+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score per eligible encounter = (numerator / denominator) expressed 0–100%. Details on cohorts for each component are specified in Table IX.D.1; full measure specifications are on the eCQI Resource Center website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator exclusion for Malnutrition Care Score
rubrics_metrics.description: The only denominator exclusion for this measure population is patients whose length of stay is less than 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals should apply the length-of-stay exclusion when determining the eligible cohort; see Table IX.D.1 for component-specific cohort definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM data source and submission — use of EHR and certified health IT
rubrics_metrics.description: The Malnutrition Care Score eCQM and other eCQMs use data collected through a hospital's electronic health record (EHR). Measures are designed to be calculated by certified health IT using patient-level data and then submitted by the PCH to CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table IX.D.2 outlines data specifications and sources for each component. PCHs must submit using the formats and specifications available on the eCQI Resource Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirements for eCQM reporting (ONC-certified health IT)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCHs must utilize health IT certified to the ONC Health IT Certification Program criteria (as adopted at 45 CFR 170.315(c)), and must use that certified health IT to calculate, export, and submit eCQM results. PCHs must use the eCQM electronic measure specifications and implementation guidance for the applicable reporting period available on the eCQI Resource Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal to codify these requirements at 42 CFR 412.24(g)(1)-(3). Health IT would not need to be recertified each time measure specifications are updated to a newer version. Substantive modernization of electronic submission methods would be proposed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format requirement — QRDA Category I
rubrics_metrics.description: PCHs must submit eCQM data via the Quality Reporting Document Architecture (QRDA) Category I (QRDA I) file format. PCHs may use third parties to submit QRDA I files on their behalf, and may use abstraction or pull data from non-certified sources to input into certified health IT for QRDA I output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect QRDA I files to reflect one patient per file per quarter and to include five identifying elements: (1) CCN; (2) CMS Program Name; (3) EHR Patient ID; (4) Reporting period in the Reporting Parameters Section; and (5) EHR Submitter ID. Refer to the QRDA Implementation Guides on the eCQI site for technical guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero denominator declaration as successful submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PCH does not have patients that meet the denominator criteria for an eCQM, the PCH may submit a zero denominator declaration, which counts as a successful submission for that eCQM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero denominator declarations allow PCHs to meet reporting requirements when no eligible patients exist. This aligns with prior CMS rules (FY2015–FY2017 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case threshold exemption policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A PCH using certified health IT would be exempt from reporting on an eCQM if the PCH has 5 or fewer applicable inpatient encounters or discharges per quarter or 20 or fewer applicable inpatient encounters or discharges per year (Medicare and non-Medicare combined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions are entered on the Denominator Declaration screen within CMS' Hospital Quality Reporting System during submission. The exemption is optional (a PCH may still report individual cases). Measures below the case threshold would not have their measure rate publicly reported. This policy aligns with other CMS quality reporting programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of technical specifications — Annual Update
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical specifications for eCQMs for the PCH Quality Reporting Program would be contained in the CMS Annual Update and implementation guidance documents (available on the eCQI Resource Center), and would generally be updated annually for code updates, logic corrections, and alignment with clinical guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCHs would be required to use the eCQM electronic measure specifications and implementation guidance for the applicable reporting period as published on the eCQI Resource Center or successor site. Annual Update process supports EHR vendors and PCHs in implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting and 30‑day preview period
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1866(k)(4) requires the Secretary to make quality measure information available to the public after PCHs have the opportunity to review their data. If adopted, CMS proposes to publicly report PCH eCQM data (e.g., Compare tool, Provider Data Catalog) after a 30-day preview period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reporting timing depends on feasibility and preview period to allow PCH review prior to public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure removal criterion — removal Factor 2 (does not align with current clinical guidelines or practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure may be removed from a program under removal Factor 2 if it does not align with current clinical guidelines or clinical practice. Example: Proposal to remove the COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage among Healthcare Personnel measure beginning with the CY 2026 reporting period/FY 2028 program year because CDC guidance moved to shared clinical decision-making and the measure no longer aligns with a single default recommendation to vaccinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considered burden vs. benefit given end of the Public Health Emergency and evolving CDC recommendations. Similar removals have been made across multiple quality reporting programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maternal Morbidity Structural measure — updated attestation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For the attestation-based Maternal Morbidity Structural measure, if a hospital answers 'yes' to participation in a Statewide and/or National Perinatal Quality Improvement Collaborative Program and implementation of patient safety practices/bundles, the hospital must also report the name of the perinatal quality improvement collaborative program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer choices remain 'yes', 'no', or 'not applicable'. Failure to provide the program name when attesting 'yes' would result in the hospital not having successfully reported all requirements for the measure and could result in a payment penalty. Reporting continues via the CMS-approved web-based HQR System once annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑Rulemaking Measure Review and conditional endorsement expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures reviewed through the Pre-Rulemaking Measure Review and Endorsement processes may be recommended or endorsed with conditions. Example: Malnutrition Care Score eCQM was recommended for adoption and endorsed with the condition that the measure steward reviews implementation data by the Spring 2029 maintenance review to examine associations with improved nutritional status or clinical endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee feedback (e.g., concerns about rural hospital staffing and whether documentation improves post-discharge outcomes) is considered; CMS and measure stewards are expected to collect and analyze implementation data in preparation for maintenance review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition strategy toward FHIR-based digital quality measures (dQMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS intends to transition eCQMs to HL7 FHIR-based eCQMs and toward a fully digital quality measure (dQM) landscape to promote interoperability and increase the value of quality measure data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a phased approach: interim expansion of eCQMs while deliberate conversion to FHIR and dQMs occurs over time. CMS references prior request for information on transition to digital quality measurement and will propose substantive modernizations in future rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCH eCQM adoption timeline and program integration
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to adopt two new eCQMs into the PCH Quality Reporting Program (Advance Care Planning eCQM and Malnutrition Care Score eCQM) for full-year reporting beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 program year, making these the first eCQMs in the PCH program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, these measures would be incorporated into PCH program reporting requirements and subject to the same certification, submission format, case threshold, zero denominator, and public reporting policies described for other programs. CMS will provide form, manner, and timing guidance (e.g., submission deadlines) on QualityNet.
